small_guidance:
- The LN kernel is already light; the bottleneck is `nn.ConvTranspose3d`. Tuning LN tile/warps further (e.g., ROWS_PER_PROG=8, num_warps=2 for C=64) will only yield marginal gains. If staying small, try ROWS_PER_PROG ∈ {2,4,8,16} with num_warps=2 and num_stages=2 since C=64 fits in one warp easily.
- Move LN normalization axis fusion into the conv-transpose epilogue once the conv is custom; for now ensure the LN input is contiguous in channels-last so the per-(N,D,H,W) row of 64 channels is contiguous (avoid the reshape copy by writing conv output channels-last).
- Add `@triton.autotune` over {(ROWS_PER_PROG=4, warps=2), (8,2), (16,4), (32,4)} keyed on N to pick the best for N=32·32·64·64≈4M rows.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.ConvTranspose3d` with a custom Triton scatter-add kernel: one program per (N, IC-tile, D_in, H_in, W_in) tile computing the input×weight outer product and atomically scattering into the (N, OC, D_out, H_out, W_out) output, handling stride=2/padding=1 in the index math. This is where >80% of the runtime sits — LN tuning cannot close the gap.
- Alternative: implement ConvTranspose3d as a gather GEMM — one program per (N, OC-tile, output-spatial tile) iterating over (IC, kD, kH, kW), computing source input coordinate `(d+pad-kd)/stride` with divisibility check; this avoids atomics and fuses LN+GELU+scale into the epilogue (since OC=64 is the LN normalization axis, accumulate full OC per output voxel in registers, then do mean/var across the 64-channel vector and apply GELU·scale before the store).
- Use channels-last (NDHWC) layout end-to-end so the 64-channel LN reduction is a contiguous register-resident reduction in the conv epilogue; this single fused kernel removes the intermediate conv-output write/read entirely.
